# Verification analysis: vlan-access-segmentation-ubuntu24

## Task

> `node1` connects `node2` on one segment and `node3` on another. Put each
> host's segment into its own VLAN on `node1` as an untagged access port, so
> the two hosts stay separated from one another while each keeps a working
> link to `node1` inside its own VLAN.

## Trial `vlan-access-segmentation-ubuntu2__c7gzua9`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor achieved the core task: node1's eth1 and eth2 were placed into separate VLANs (10 and 20) as untagged/PVID access ports via a Linux VLAN-aware bridge, after correctly diagnosing that SONiC-VS's native config-CLI VLAN member commands could not bind the real virtio NICs. Both node2 and node3 retain working pings to node1 within their own VLAN, and cross-segment isolation was rigorously proven (including the same-subnet ARP-INCOMPLETE test, not just differing subnets). All three nodes were individually rebooted with clear boot-identity changes, and VLAN, connectivity, and isolation state were all re-verified as recovered afterward, satisfying the restart evidence protocol. The only notable hygiene issues are a leftover orphaned VLAN 10/20 entry in SONiC's config database (unrelated to the working bridge-based mechanism) and an unexplained new failed service on node1 after reboot.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.720 | 0.900 | 50/2 (+11 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** node1's link to node2 (eth1) is placed into its own VLAN as an untagged access port
  - **Why:** SONiC-VS's native `config vlan member add` CLI rejected the real eth1/eth2 NICs (cmd-9e3cf90838634d63: 'eth1 does not exist', because configdb only recognizes Ethernet0..127 aliases, confirmed by cmd-a8608794bdee4bd2). The executor instead built a VLAN-aware Linux bridge (br0), enslaved eth1, and set it PVID/untagged in VLAN 10 (cmd-7e91a6ab79694441, cmd-3910d7355ea749c3, cmd-3da4d2739b264b1f), which is a reasonable adaptation given the platform constraint and functions as an access port. Confirmed present again after node1's reboot (cmd-89ed88a578314933).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-9e3cf90838634d63`, `cmd-a8608794bdee4bd2`, `cmd-7e91a6ab79694441`, `cmd-3910d7355ea749c3`, `cmd-3da4d2739b264b1f`, `cmd-89ed88a578314933`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** node1's link to node3 (eth2) is placed into its own, different VLAN as an untagged access port
  - **Why:** Same bridge-based mechanism enslaved eth2 and set it PVID/untagged in VLAN 20, distinct from eth1's VLAN 10 (cmd-3da4d2739b264b1f). Re-verified intact after node1 reboot (cmd-89ed88a578314933).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3da4d2739b264b1f`, `cmd-fd9389ddd5134408`, `cmd-89ed88a578314933`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** node2 keeps a working link to node1 inside its own VLAN
  - **Why:** node2 successfully pinged node1's VLAN10 gateway IP (192.168.201.1) both before and after all three nodes were rebooted (cmd-246069b1b4204bb9, cmd-f5af88114b674a72, cmd-b9241e5787dd4e9e), demonstrating a working, persistent access-port link.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-246069b1b4204bb9`, `cmd-f5af88114b674a72`, `cmd-b9241e5787dd4e9e`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** node3 keeps a working link to node1 inside its own VLAN
  - **Why:** node3 successfully pinged node1's VLAN20 gateway IP (192.168.202.1) both before and after all three nodes were rebooted (cmd-0075b5b6488e4b5c, cmd-cb56f9a0108446f8, cmd-59ecee9bc26b4a79).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0075b5b6488e4b5c`, `cmd-cb56f9a0108446f8`, `cmd-59ecee9bc26b4a79`
- **req-5 — Satisfied:** node2 and node3 stay separated from one another (VLAN isolation, not merely subnet mismatch)
  - **Why:** node3 was given an address inside node2's own subnet (192.168.201.3) to rule out isolation being a subnet-numbering artifact; node2's ping to that address showed 100% loss with an INCOMPLETE ARP entry (cmd-71605834016a4d85, cmd-189052d39a26482c), proving true L2/VLAN separation. The same test was repeated after all three nodes rebooted with the same result (cmd-a181a5c41113460b, cmd-96bac714f5924c78), and the temporary address was removed afterward (cmd-2880f88612494b0a, cmd-4707a1e203854ad6).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-71605834016a4d85`, `cmd-189052d39a26482c`, `cmd-2880f88612494b0a`, `cmd-a181a5c41113460b`, `cmd-96bac714f5924c78`, `cmd-4707a1e203854ad6`
- **req-6 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: each managed node shows healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered VLAN/connectivity/isolation state
  - **Why:** For each of node1, node2, node3: a pre-reboot boot_id and healthy baseline was captured (cmd-29afaf6371cb4303/cmd-aad1a2d199f2401d/cmd-cfd3ba69ee774b4a, corroborated by fixed global:before_prepare boot-identity snapshots), a reboot was issued, a different post-reboot boot_id was confirmed (cmd-b00b70a8d1ba4d51, cmd-fcf334dfe0f44667, cmd-e8d94df5bda24ff4, corroborated by fixed global:after_executor boot-identity snapshots), and the VLAN bridge (auto-recreated by the systemd oneshot unit), static IPs (via systemd-networkd drop-ins), connectivity, and cross-segment isolation were all re-verified afterward (cmd-89ed88a578314933, cmd-b9241e5787dd4e9e, cmd-59ecee9bc26b4a79, cmd-96bac714f5924c78). node1's segmentation service ran itself to completion after boot without manual intervention (cmd-a5e146323a6f491c).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-29afaf6371cb4303`, `cmd-aad1a2d199f2401d`, `cmd-cfd3ba69ee774b4a`, `cmd-dc182d10c52f47ed`, `cmd-b00b70a8d1ba4d51`, `cmd-0b6265146d224594`, `cmd-fcf334dfe0f44667`, `cmd-0a90b6d8a8d141a5`, `cmd-e8d94df5bda24ff4`, `cmd-89ed88a578314933`, `cmd-a5e146323a6f491c`, `cmd-b9241e5787dd4e9e`, `cmd-59ecee9bc26b4a79`, `cmd-96bac714f5924c78`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.720**. Most exploratory mutations during link-mapping (temporary IPs on eth1/eth2 and enp8s0 in cmd-061ddb657e294768/cmd-40318b72cddb4481/cmd-20b68f9d5df9499a, and a brief systemd-networkd stop on node2/node3) were bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted or superseded by the final persistent config (cmd-66de0c07521c4023, cmd-2b2e2e25de1c4afe, cmd-ed9bde532a534285 restarting networkd). One unnecessary mutation was left unreverted: cmd-9e3cf90838634d63 ran `config vlan add 10` and `config vlan add 20` against SONiC's config database before discovering that `config vlan member add` could not bind eth1/eth2; the executor pivoted to a Linux-bridge-based implementation but never removed the now-orphaned, memberless VLAN 10/20 entries left in configdb, which are dead/confusing residue alongside the real (bridge-based) mechanism. Additionally, after node1's reboot a previously-absent failed unit, system-health.service, appeared and was not investigated or remediated; this is plausibly an inherent SONiC-VS reboot artifact rather than something the VLAN change caused, but the executor did not confirm this or leave a note about it.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-9e3cf90838634d63`, `cmd-061ddb657e294768`, `cmd-40318b72cddb4481`, `cmd-20b68f9d5df9499a`, `cmd-66de0c07521c4023`, `cmd-2b2e2e25de1c4afe`, `cmd-ed9bde532a534285`

### Comments and limitations

- The final VLAN mechanism relies on a Linux bridge rather than SONiC's native VLAN configuration subsystem, due to a platform limitation in this SONiC-VS image; functionally equivalent but architecturally different from how VLANs would be configured on real SONiC hardware.
- The cause of the new post-reboot failed unit (system-health.service) on node1 was not investigated, so it is unclear whether it is a pre-existing platform quirk or a side effect of the executor's changes.
- Orphaned, memberless VLAN 10/20 entries were left in SONiC's config database from the initial (unsuccessful) native-CLI attempt; they are inert but not cleaned up.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.720); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
